name: DEAD-box helicase 3 X-linked
pathways: negative regulation of non-canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction

function.text: DDX3X encodes ATP-dependent RNA helicase DDX3X. Annotated molecular activities include transcription factor binding and CTPase activity. It participates in intracellular signal transduction and negative regulation of non-canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to X-linked syndromic intellectual disability (x-linked); intellectual disability, X-linked 102 (x-linked).

somatic.text: Reported somatic alteration contexts include Aggressive NK-cell leukemia; Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma; Cribriform adenocarcinoma of salivary gland. The alteration class and exact variant must be assessed in the disease context.

function.text: DDX3X encodes ATP-dependent RNA helicase DDX3X. Based in part on similarity, the ATPase activity can be stimulated by various ribo-and deoxynucleic acids indicative for a relaxed substrate specificity. It binds RNA G-quadruplex (rG4s) structures, including those located in the 5'-UTR of NRAS mRNA. It positively regulates CDKN1A/WAF1/CIP1 transcription in an SP1-dependent manner, hence inhibits cell growth.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with X-linked syndromic intellectual disability (x-linked); intellectual disability, X-linked 102 (x-linked).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving DDX3X have been reported in aggressive NK-cell leukemia, extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, and cribriform adenocarcinoma of salivary gland.
